prompt:
A C API works in plain `double` metres:

```c
double meters_add(double a, double b);
double meters_scale(double m, double k);
```

I want to implement it in Rust with a type-safe unit wrapper. Define a tuple-struct newtype `pub struct Meters(pub f64);` (derive `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq`) that is guaranteed to have the same size, alignment AND function-call ABI as a bare `f64`, so it can appear directly in `extern "C"` signatures while C keeps declaring plain `double`. Then export exactly:

- `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn meters_add(a: Meters, b: Meters) -> Meters` (the sum)
- `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn meters_scale(m: Meters, k: f64) -> Meters` (the product)

Answer with a single ```rust code block containing the library code (no `main`).
notes: The improper_ctypes_definitions probe in the grader is what catches a newtype with no repr. A #[repr(C)] newtype is also FFI-safe to the lint; it is NOT ABI-identical to f64 on Windows x64 (an 8-byte struct travels in an integer register) and the f64-declared calls catch that there, but on SysV x86-64 the two ABIs coincide and a repr(C) answer would pass. Verified on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc only.
